operation.description:
MUTATING operation. Verify target and authorized intent; reconcile outcome before retry. Update an existing **Unit Template** (v2 native-entity API).

`PUT https://{subdomain}.daftra.com/v2/api/entity/unit_template/{id}`

## URL rules

- **The record id goes in the path.** `/v2/api/entity/unit_template` without an id is the
  *collection* path — it only accepts `POST` (create). A `PUT` there returns
  `405 The PUT method is not supported for route api/entity/unit_template. Supported methods: POST.`
- **No trailing slash.** A URL ending in `/` is answered with a `301` to the same URL without it,
  and HTTP clients drop the request method **and body** when they follow a `301` — the call arrives
  as a `GET` and you get a misleading "The GET method is not supported" error. Never combine
  `curl --location` with `--request PUT`.

## Authentication

`Authorization: Bearer <access_token>` from the OAuth password grant. The `apikey` header belongs to
the v1 CakePHP `/api2` API and is ignored on this surface.

## Body semantics

- **`id` in the body is what makes this an update.** Omit it and the request **inserts a new record**
  and returns the new id — the `{id}` in the URL does not prevent that. Always send `id`, matching the URL.
- Fields you omit keep their stored value (partial merge)…
- …**except `active`, which is a checkbox: omitting it stores `0`.** Send it on every update.
- `branch_id` and `staff_id` are assigned by the server (auto-branch / auto-staff) and ignored if sent.
- `created` / `modified` are read-only.

## Unit factors

- The array key is **`unit_templates_unit_factors`** (parent table + subform name). `unit_factors`
  is silently ignored — the rows are dropped without an error.
- The array **replaces the whole set**: a row **with** `id` is updated, a row **without** `id` is
  inserted, and any existing row you leave out is **deleted**.
- Omit the key entirely to leave the existing factors untouched.

## Responses

| Code | Body | When |
| ---- | ---- | ---- |
| 200 | `{message, id}` | Saved. `message` is localised to the site language — match on the status and `id`, not the text. |
| 400 | `{message}` or `{message, errors}` | `Record not found` for an unknown id, or `Entity not saved` with per-field errors. |
| 401 | `{error}` | Caller lacks the update permission for this entity. |
| 405 | `{message}` | Wrong method for the path — usually a missing id or a followed trailing-slash redirect (see *URL rules*). |

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Id of the Unit Template to update. Send the same value in the body `id`.

id.description: Id of the Unit Template to update. Must match the {id} in the URL. If omitted, a NEW record is created instead of updating.

active.description: 1 = active, 0 = inactive. Checkbox field — if you omit it, it is stored as 0.

main_unit_name.description: Name of the main (base) unit, e.g. gram.

unit_small_name.description: Short name of the main unit, e.g. g.

unit_templates_unit_factors.description: Full set of unit factors after the update. A row with `id` is updated, a row without `id` is inserted, and any existing row omitted from this array is deleted. Omit the whole key to leave the existing factors untouched.

id.description: Id of an existing factor row to update. Omit to insert a new row.

factor.description: How many main units this factor equals, e.g. 1000.

small_name.description: Short name of the factor, e.g. kg.

200.description: Saved. `message` is localised to the site language, so match on the status code and `id` rather than the text. A response whose `id` differs from the one you sent means the body `id` was missing and a new record was created.

400.description: Unknown id (`Record not found`) or a rejected payload (`Entity not saved`).

errors.description: Present for validation failures: field key → list of messages.

401.description: The authenticated user lacks the update permission for this entity.
